cases.title: Local daemon resource access posture
cases.prompt: Should the local daemon expose resource access URLs outside localhost by default?

runs.label: Deliberum structured run
runs.outputSummary: Preserve localhost defaults, require explicit non-local opt-in, and keep access tokens out of the semantic ledger.

runs.label: Direct answer baseline
runs.outputSummary: Recommend configurable resource URLs with a short note about HTTPS.

runs.label: Central judge baseline
runs.outputSummary: Collect two suggestions, then produce a single deployment recommendation.

findings.evidence: The Deliberum run preserved bearer access id leakage and non-local base URL opt-in as explicit risks; the direct baseline mentioned HTTPS but did not require non-local opt-in.
The Deliberum output references resource delivery and grant lifecycle events, while the direct baseline has no provenance trail.
The direct baseline is shorter, but the Deliberum run includes concrete daemon env gates and testable deployment constraints.
Both runs identified remote access risk, but the judge baseline compressed token handling into a single deployment recommendation.
The Deliberum run keeps objections, policy decisions, and implementation checks separately traceable.
The Deliberum run produced concrete env names and validation expectations; the judge baseline stayed at recommendation level.

cases.title: Provider setup without secret leakage
cases.prompt: How should a local pre-production operator configure provider-backed participants without exposing secrets?

runs.label: Deliberum structured run
runs.outputSummary: Use safe runtime profile metadata and comment-only env templates; keep secrets in daemon runtime environment.

runs.label: Multi-perspective prompt baseline
runs.outputSummary: Summarize developer, operator, and security perspectives in one response.

runs.label: Role-agent workflow baseline
runs.outputSummary: Ask security and operator agents for recommendations, then merge them.

findings.evidence: The Deliberum run kept secret leakage objections as unresolved guardrails instead of turning them into optional advice.
Both runs preserve a security perspective, but the multi-perspective prompt does not attach it to later implementation checks.
The multi-perspective baseline is easier to read, while the Deliberum run gives more explicit setup boundaries.
The Deliberum run records objections and decisions as public process material; the role-agent baseline merges them into a final recommendation.
The Deliberum run preserves dissent around interactive setup scope, while the role-agent baseline collapses the operator path into one merged answer.
Both outputs are understandable but emphasize different tradeoffs.

cases.title: Final audit readiness
cases.prompt: When should a deliberation run proceed from accepted candidates to final audit and outcome compilation?

runs.label: Deliberum structured run
runs.outputSummary: Require final candidate proposal material, explicit audit findings, unresolved limits, and provenance before compilation.

runs.label: Independent answers summary baseline
runs.outputSummary: Collect independent answers and summarize the strongest common recommendation.

runs.label: Voting aggregation baseline
runs.outputSummary: Ask participants to vote on final readiness and summarize the majority position.

findings.evidence: The Deliberum run preserves unresolved conditions and audit findings in the compiled projection; the summary baseline smooths them into a single recommendation.
Both outputs avoid unsupported factual claims, but the Deliberum projection keeps evidence needs visible.
The Deliberum run links audit material to final candidate proposal events, while the summary baseline cannot trace readiness decisions.
The Deliberum run treats readiness as audited conditions; the voting baseline treats majority agreement as sufficient.
The Deliberum run keeps factual uncertainty and evidence needs explicit, while the voting baseline can pass unsupported majority claims forward.
The Deliberum run has event-level provenance for final audit readiness; the voting baseline reports aggregate preference only.

cases.title: Cost and latency transparency
cases.prompt: How should a deliberation system account for extra provider calls and latency without hiding the quality tradeoff?

runs.label: Deliberum structured run
runs.outputSummary: Expose provider call count, event count, and unresolved quality tradeoffs instead of presenting extra deliberation as free.

runs.label: Direct answer baseline
runs.outputSummary: Return a concise answer with one provider call and no explicit deliberation overhead.

runs.label: Multi-perspective prompt baseline
runs.outputSummary: Ask one model to compare several perspectives in one request and summarize the tradeoff.

findings.evidence: The direct answer baseline used one provider call, while the Deliberum run used seven provider calls to preserve objections, audit material, and provenance.
notes: Lower cost is a legitimate baseline advantage when the task does not need deliberation depth.

findings.evidence: The direct answer completed faster because it did not run sealed divergence, review, or final audit stages.
The multi-perspective baseline used one prompt to approximate several viewpoints, while the Deliberum run paid for separate proposal and audit material.
The multi-perspective prompt returned sooner, but the Deliberum run exposed where extra latency came from through event and provider-call metadata.
